findings.title: Missing re-check after acquiring write lock causes redundant manifest loads
findings.body: After the read lock finds the cache empty, the code takes the write lock but does not check `entryPointAssetsCache` again. When the cache is cold, several concurrent requests can all miss under RLock. Each then takes the write lock in turn and re-reads and re-parses the manifest from disk or the CDN. This is wasted work, and the cached pointer gets replaced several times. Add a double-check after `Lock()`: if not in Dev mode and the cache is non-nil, return it.

findings.title: Load failure overwrites a previously cached value with nil
findings.body: `entryPointAssetsCache = result` runs even when loading fails, in which case `result` is nil. In Dev mode, a single transient read or parse error, for example while the frontend build is rewriting the manifest, wipes out the good cached value. Only assign the cache when `err == nil`.
